item__Input_question: I’m really struggling with the side effects of Tolvaptan. is there a treatment that works better and is easier on my body, and would I still see the benefits even if I had to stop taking it for a while?

I’ve had this disease for years and already have quite a few cysts. is there suggest the drug could still help me if I start treatment later, or is it only for people who are just starting to show symptoms?

I’m really nervous about the 'black box' liver warning on Tolvaptan, and honestly, the constant thirst and bathroom trips are exhausting. I read about a drug called Cinacalcet that’s already being used for other bone and kidney issues, could that be a safer way to slow down my cysts without trashing my liver?
Could I take Cinacalcet AND Tolvaptan together? Would they work as a team to shrink my cysts even faster?

I feel like I’m constantly fighting two different battles: one to keep my blood pressure down and another to stop these cysts from growing. I'm worried that my current blood pressure meds are just a 'band-aid.' is there a way to fix that root cause instead of just treating the symptoms?

If the genetic 'blueprint' for my child's kidney disease is completely missing—the worst-case scenario—why is it that their liver shows clear signs of disease, but their kidneys look almost completely normal? Does this mean there is something 'protecting' the kidneys that we can use to develop a treatment, and should I be worried about other parts of the body, like the eyes or teeth, that we haven't checked before?"

I know that PKD is usually described as a problem with how my kidney cells 'sense' things on the outside. But is it possible that the disease is actually deeper than that, ike a problem with how my cells create and use energy on the inside? If it is an energy problem, could my diet or my metabolism actually change how fast my cysts grow?
Are there medicines that could slow cyst growth instead of just treating symptoms?
Even when I try to do everything right, like watching my diet and taking my medications, my kidneys still seem to be getting bigger. What could be driving that growth at a cellular level?

I understand that my polycystic kidney disease is genetic, but even when I follow my treatment plan and take care of myself, my kidneys still seem to keep getting worse. I want to understand what’s actually happening inside my kidney cells that causes the cysts to grow. Are there specific processes or signals in the cells that doctors could eventually target to slow the disease down in a way that would improve my long-term quality of life and delay kidney failure?

’ve always heard that acetaminophen mainly damages the liver, and that the antidote NAC is supposed to protect people after an overdose. But I’ve also read that some patients still end up with kidney problems even when they get treated. I want to understand why my kidneys might be affected differently than my liver. What is actually happening inside kidney cells during an overdose, and why doesn’t the usual antidote work for the kidneys? Are there other treatments that might better protect kidney cells and reduce long-term damage?
I heard that certain kidney proteins can affect how cells use energy. Could this make my child’s cysts worse, and is there a way to help prevent that?

I was reading about how kidneys in PKD don't just get cysts—they basically get 'choked out' by internal scarring. I’m curious, is there any research into stopping that scarring process directly? It feels like if we could just clear out those scar-forming cells, the healthy parts of my kidney might actually have a chance to breathe.

my kidney cells 'forget' they are adult cells and start acting like they're still growing in a fetus. Is there a way to flip the switch back to 'adult mode' so my kidneys stop producing these cysts and just focus on filtering my blood?

If the 'immune cells' in my body right now are actually setting the stage for how my kidneys and liver will look in 10 years, is there a way to 're-train' them today so they stop building scars and start helping instead?"

I keep hearing that when cells get damaged, they’re supposed to stop dividing to protect the body. How does a damaged cell actually ‘decide’ to shut itself down, and why does that process sometimes fail in diseases or aging?

I know my blood work looks 'fine' right now, but I can feel that things are changing. If there’s actually a point where this disease suddenly 'shifts gears' and starts moving faster, can we use these better scans to see if I’m hitting that moment right now? I don’t want to wait until my kidneys are already failing to finally start doing something about it.

I have polycystic kidney disease, and I keep hearing that inflammation might make my cysts grow faster. Why is my immune system involved in a genetic kidney disease, and could calming inflammation actually help slow the disease down?
What did patients with ADPKD say helped them stay healthy during the COVID, and what made things harder?
I have liver disease and heard that some genetic changes can happen in the liver over time. Does that always mean cancer, or can some changes actually be protective?
have polycystic kidney disease, and I keep hearing about proteins in the kidney that can be both helpful and harmful. How can something slow cyst growth but still make kidney scarring worse?

I’ve been told that ADPKD causes my kidney cells to grow and divide when they shouldn’t. I read that some of these cells have problems when they divide and that new treatments might be able to stop those abnormal cells from surviving. Can you explain how stopping these unhealthy kidney cells from dividing could slow cyst growth and actually improve kidney function, without harming normal kidney cells?
If inflammation is part of what’s damaging my kidneys, why hasn’t it been treated more directly before, and could targeting something to help protect kidney function long term?
If inflammation in my kidneys is sending signals to my brain, could that be making my condition worse without me realizing it?

I was told my polycystic kidney disease is caused by a small change in a gene, not a missing gene. Does that kind of genetic change affect how my kidney cells work, and does it mean there could be treatments that help the protein work better instead of just slowing the disease?

I have polycystic kidney disease, and I’m scared of how it keeps getting worse over time. Does this research mean there might be new treatments that can stop cysts from starting in the first place, not just slow them down after they grow?

I have polycystic kidney disease, and I’m worried about how it keeps getting worse over time. I heard that researchers are studying kidney cells in a very detailed way to see what changes first as cysts grow. Could this kind of research actually help doctors catch the disease earlier or choose treatments that are better for me personally in the future?

I have ADPKD and I’m worried about losing kidney function as my cysts grow. This research talks about a protein that might explain why kidney function gets worse. Does this mean doctors might someday be able to slow kidney damage even if cysts are already there, or monitor my risk of kidney failure more accurately?
Could differences in how kidney samples are processed explain why treatments don’t always work the same for everyone with kidney disease?

If I or my child has polycystic kidney disease, how can doctors tell how fast the disease might get worse, and what signs or tests matter most when deciding how closely we should be monitored or treated?
How can understanding the genetic cause and type of polycystic kidney disease I have help my care team personalize my treatment, monitoring, and future planning for kidney health?
Because ADPKD needs long-term treatment, how are new drugs being designed to protect my kidneys without causing problems in the rest of my body?

I’ve been told my polycystic kidney disease is related to problems with tiny structures in my kidney cells called cilia—how does that actually cause cysts to form, and does understanding this help doctors find better treatments for patients like me?

I’ve learned that polycystic kidney disease can affect more than just my kidneys and that there are new genetic tests and imaging tools how can these advances help personalize my care and predict how my disease might progress?

My kidney function tests are still mostly normal, but my doctor keeps ordering imaging tests how can advanced imaging, beyond just measuring kidney size, help predict how my disease might progress and guide my treatment?
I have polycystic kidney disease and I keep hearing about diets like fasting or keto, are these actually safe for me, and what kind of diet should I realistically follow to protect my kidneys?
What are the key genetic and cellular mechanisms underlying autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, and how do they inform diagnosis and treatment?
I’m worried about how surgery might affect my future kidney transplant. How can we decide together whether removing a kidney now is the best choice for me?

My child is at risk for ADPKD, and I understand there are different ways to monitor or screen for the disease. How do we decide whether to do ongoing surveillance versus immediate genetic or ultrasound testing? Also, what steps can we take at home, such as diet or lifestyle changes, to help manage the disease and protect their kidneys?

My child has been diagnosed with ARPKD, and I understand that the disease can vary widely in severity depending on the specific gene mutation. How does knowing whether the mutation is in PKHD1 or DZIP1L help guide my child’s care? Are there specific treatments, monitoring strategies, or lifestyle changes we should focus on based on their genetic profile?

I know that ADPKD can affect more than just my kidneys, including causing pain, depression, heart problems, and liver or pancreatic cysts. How will my care team monitor and manage these issues alongside my kidney function? Are there specific tools or resources to help me track my pain, mood, or other symptoms, and how can we work together to make sure these concerns are addressed during my appointments?

As someone living with ADPKD, I’m concerned about how my experiences and daily challenges are taken into account. How can I make sure that my symptoms, pain levels, mental health, and overall quality of life are properly monitored and included in my care?

Can you explain what potential new therapies are being studied, how TKV is used to measure their effectiveness, and whether these new drugs might address symptoms that really affect daily life, like pain, fatigue, or cyst-related complications? Also, how long might it take for these therapies to become available for patients like me?

If my cells have lost the ability to clean out their own broken parts, is there anything I can actually do maybe through my diet or by fixing my gut health to help them start 'recycling' again? I want to know if I can help my kidneys clear out the gunk before it turns into more cysts.
I read about folate-conjugated nanoparticles that deliver rapamycin directly to polycystic kidneys. Could this approach reduce side effects and improve kidney function for people with PKD?

a study tested whether drinking a prescribed amount of water could slow kidney cyst growth in ADPKD. As a patient, I’m wondering: does increasing my daily water intake actually help protect my kidneys or slow disease progression?

diet especially high-carbohydrate intake, might affect the progression of ADPKD. As a patient, I’m wondering: could following a low-carb or ketogenic diet help slow my kidney cyst growth or support my kidney health alongside my current treatment?
